title: CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss: ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’
description:
Recently-appointed CBS News correspondent Trevor Phillips has given a typically forthright assessment of his new boss, Bari Weiss.

	“Bari and her t
body:
Recently-appointed CBS News correspondent Trevor Phillips has given a typically forthright assessment of his new boss, Bari Weiss.

	“Bari and her team have a huge tanker of a network news organisation to turn around, and they are assembling a little team on the bridge,” he told The Daily Telegraph. “The great thing about her is that she’s one of those people who will either change the world or crash and burn. But when they crash and burn, it’s in technicolour.”
	

	Phillips, who has been a correspondent for the U.K.’s Sky News since 2021, was handpicked by CBS News editor-in-chief Weiss to join the Paramount-owned network as senior global affairs correspondent. He will also join “60 Minutes.” A veteran writer and broadcaster as well as a former politician, Phillips was previously chair of the U.K.’s Equality and Human Rights Commission and in 2022 was knighted for his services to equality and human rights .


	He is set to move across the pond this summer to take up the new role at CBS. “You know, I’m 72. It’s a great adventure,” he said of Weiss’s offer. “And who turns down adventures if someone is willing to take a chance on you?”

	To mark the move, Phillips gave a wide-ranging interview to the Telegraph, in which he gamely discussed some of the controversy that has swirled since Weiss was appointed to her role last year. “In the U.S., the controversy has been framed as, ‘CBS News is becoming anti-woke’. But that’s not what Bari is about,” Phillip said. “She has her own views, some of which I’m sympathetic to, some of which I’m not, but her point is that the media should be heterodox. There should be a variety of voices.”
	

	He wouldn’t comment on rumors that reporter Holly Williams, who works in CBS News’ London bureau, had been taken off an interview with right wing politician Nigel Farage in favor of Phillips, but said: “What’s interesting in politics now is this current of thought, represented by Farage, Giorgia Meloni and Marine Le Pen, which essentially says the way we have done conventional politics is bust in a new world, and we need to do things differently. We keep trying to fit it into the old Right/Left duopoly, and I don’t think that’s quite right. The interviews I’m interested in doing will include that group [of leaders].”

	“I’m not the smoothest presenter on television or reader of the autocue, but I guess they think that I manage the chaos [of live guests] well,” Phillips added. “Broadcast journalism has, to some extent, become the creature of entertainment. We need to return to the business of reporting. To put it in its crassest terms, the story needs to come before the reporter. Too many people who do what I do put themselves between the viewer and the story, and that’s not our job.”

schema.headline: CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss: ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’

title: ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On ‘As Planned’ After Ariana Grande Exits
description:
The London production of “Sunday in the Park With George” is set to go ahead as planned despite Ariana Grande exiting the show.

	The Stephen Sondhe
body:
The London production of “Sunday in the Park With George” is set to go ahead as planned despite Ariana Grande exiting the show.

	The Stephen Sondheim revival, which also stars Grande’s “Wicked” co-star Jonathan Bailey, was scheduled to premiere at London’s Barbican next summer with producers set to launch ticket sales after Grande completed the last leg of her “The Eternal Sunshine Tour” on Sept. 1 in the U.K.


	However, on Sunday night reps for the actress said Grande will be “taking a step back from visibility” after she completes her tour — which includes dropping out of the play.
	

	But the show must go on and a rep for producers Empire Street Productions tells Variety: “The production will open at the Barbican in summer 2027 as planned, and casting will be announced in due course.”

	Grande was set to star as both Dot and Marie in the revival opposite Bailey as painter George Seurat, offering “Wicked” fans a rare opportunity to see the film’s stars together live on stage. “Sunday in the Park With George” is directed by Tony and Olivier Award winner Marianne Elliot, with design by Tom Scutt. Auditions for the ensemble have been taking place in London this summer.

	Producers for the show said they “wish [Grande] nothing but the best,” adding: “We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support.”

	In recent years fans have expressed increasing concern for Grande, particularly in regards to her physical appearance. The actor and singer previously disclosed she was diagnosed with PTSD after a suicide bomber killed 22 people, including a number of children, at her concert in Manchester in 2017.
	

	Aside from “Sunday in the Park With George,” Grande’s only other publicly-known commitment is a role in upcoming Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller comedy “Focker-in-Law,” which is set to bow over Thanksgiving. It is unclear whether Grande will still participate in the film’s publicity tour.

	Grande’s rep told People magazine: “She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny.”

schema.headline: ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On ‘As Planned’ After Ariana Grande Exits

title: ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission
description: “Peaky Blinders” may have given closely clipped back and sides haircuts a new lease of life, but it’s now helped a region of the U.K. land official
body:
“Peaky Blinders” may have given closely clipped back and sides haircuts a new lease of life, but it’s now helped a region of the U.K. land official backing as a center for high-end productions. 

	The British Film Commission has announced that the West Midlands, home to the city of Birmingham and where “Peaky Blinders” is set and shot, has been named the U.K.’s eighth official regional production hub for scripted inward investment for film and high-end TV. 
	

	According to the Commission, having served as production base for “Peaky Blinders,” the feature film “The Immortal Man” and the as-yet untitled “Peaky Blinders” spin-off series, the region has now fulfilled the criteria needed to receive official hub status. 


	The West Midlands joins South-West England (Bristol); North-West England (Manchester and Liverpool); Yorkshire (Leeds); Northern Ireland (Belfast); Scotland (Glasgow and Edinburgh); Wales (Cardiff); and London & South-East England as an official production hub, lending its strength to a UK-wide offer which contributed £5.8 billion ($7.8 billion) to the UK economy in 2025. 

	“As Tommy Shelby of the Peaky Blinders once said, ‘when you plan something well, there’s no need to rush.’ The growing success of the West Midlands as a U.K. production hub certainly bears this out. Over the course of nearly 15 years, the region has steadily grown in strength and stature, building skills, infrastructure and reputation,” said Adrian Wootton, Chief Executive of the British Film Commission.

	“With the West Midlands becoming an official regional production hub, our offer to the global film and TV industry now spans the length and breadth of the U.K.: wherever you base your production, you’re within a stone’s throw of world-class facilities, crew and talent, with access to one-of-a-kind locations and some of the world’s most stable, transparent and generous tax incentives.”
	

	The two upcoming “Peaky Blinders” spin-off series are being film at the recently opened in Birmingham’s Digbeth Loc. Studios, which was founded by show creator Steven Knight. 

	“I’m thrilled that the West Midlands has been recognised as a fantastic place to make film and TV,” said Knight. The opening of Digbeth Loc. Studios is an important part of that ambition, providing a home for world-class film and television production in the heart of Birmingham. We are at the beginning of a journey, and we’ve got off to a great start. The West Midlands is always ambitious, and we believe we will create a global content making industry in our neighbourhood.”

	In addition to the region’s new hub status, the BBC previously announced plans to establish its future regional headquarters in The Tea Factory in Digbeth .

schema.headline: ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission

title: Action Man Movie, Based on Iconic British Toy Originally Inspired by ‘G.I. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro
description:
Action Man — the iconic British action figure that first launched in 1966 — is getting the movie treatment.

	Variety has confirmed that an Action M
body:
Action Man — the iconic British action figure that first launched in 1966 — is getting the movie treatment.

	Variety has confirmed that an Action Man film is being developed by U.K. powerhouse studio Working Title alongside Hasbro, who own the licence and whose own G.I. Joe toyline the original Action Man was based on. 

	The script for the project is being written by LA-based U.K. filmmaker Simon Hatt, known for his work at Marvel including as an exec producer on “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3,” and “X-Men ’97” co-writer Anthony Sellitti.
	

	Producing is Jeremy Latchem, another former Marvel exec whose credits include “Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves,” “Spider-Man: Homecoming” and “Avenger: Age of Ultron.”


	Action Man, launched in the U.K. by Palitoy, was originally based on Hasbro’s 1964 G.I. Joe figure, but later models gave it a more local look and feel, with uniforms and accessories reflecting British armed forces. It was reintroduced in 1993, based on the G.I. Joe Hall of Fame figure of that time, while in 2006 Hasbro licensed reproductions of a variety of the original Action Man figures to celebrate its 40th anniversary. Action Man did get its own animated cartoon series, but this was only available on video in the U.K. due to broadcasting rules regarding advertising to children.

	G.I. Joe, meanwhile, has already had three live-action movies, starting with 2009’s “G.I. Joe: The Rise of the Cobra,” which grossed $302 million worldwide, followed by “G.I. Joe: Retaliation” ($375.7 million) in 2013 and the 2021 reboot “Snake Eyes,” which made just $40 million off a budget between $88-110 million. A fourth film, “G.I. Joe: Ever Vigilant,” was in development but has since stalled. 
	

	Variety‘s sister publication The Hollywood Reporter was the first to announce the Action Man movie

schema.headline: Action Man Movie, Based on Iconic British Toy Originally Inspired by ‘G.I. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro

title: Zee Shareholders Approve $330 Million Capital Raise Before Indian Regulator Bars Company From Markets
description: Shareholders of Indian media giant Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. approved a promoter group fund infusion worth INR3143.5 crore ($330 million) a
body:
Shareholders of Indian media giant Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. approved a promoter group fund infusion worth INR3143.5 crore ($330 million) and a new employee stock option plan at an extraordinary general meeting, a day before India’s securities regulator barred the company and two of its top executives from the market.

	The Mumbai-headquartered media and technology company said its shareholders backed a preferential issue of 249,485,563 warrants to a promoter group entity, priced at INR126 ($1.32) each. A warrant gives its holder the right to convert it into a company share at a later date, at a price fixed now. Once exercised, the promoters’ stake will grow to 23.79% of the company.
	

	Shareholders also cleared the “Truly Yours” employee stock option plan, under which 37,422,835 stock options with a face value of INR1 ($0.01) each will be granted to eligible employees of Zee and its subsidiaries, in one or more tranches.


	R. Gopalan, chair of Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd., thanked shareholders for their support. “This approval is a clear reflection of the shareholders’ belief in the Company and its management,” Gopalan said. “The board firmly believes that robust growth capital coupled with enhanced promoter alignment, will serve as key enablers in ensuring long-term profitability in a dynamic business environment.”

	A day after the shareholder vote, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) – the country’s capital markets watchdog – issued an order barring Zee from the securities market for two months and barring chair emeritus Subhash Chandra and managing director and CEO Punit Goenka from the market for 12 months each. SEBI also imposed penalties totaling INR1.48 crore ($155,000), split between INR30 lakh ($31,000) on Zee, INR58 lakh ($61,000) on Goenka and INR60 lakh ($63,000) on Chandra.
	

	The order concerns the pledge of a Zee-owned property in Hyderabad, used in December 2018 to secure INR726 crore ($76.1 million) in loans for four entities linked to Essel Group, the promoter group associated with Chandra and Goenka. SEBI found the pledge was never disclosed to or approved by Zee’s board or audit committee, and determined that Chandra and Goenka had used the company’s asset to shield borrowings tied to their own family-controlled entities.

	A company spokesperson said Zee was reviewing the order with legal counsel and did not expect it to affect the fund-raising exercise. “The company would like to clarify that pursuant to the regulatory approvals received from the stock exchanges and from its esteemed shareholders at the Extraordinary General Meeting conducted on 31st July 2026, it will further take all required steps to successfully complete the fund-raising exercise, which is aimed at strengthening its financial foundation, and will also continue to work towards creating value for its stakeholders,” the spokesperson said.

	The order is the latest in a long-running SEBI probe into Zee’s promoters. The regulator first barred Goenka and Chandra from holding managerial or directorial roles at listed companies in June 2023, over allegations of fund diversion. The Securities Appellate Tribunal set aside that order that October, but the scrutiny continued to shadow Zee’s proposed $10 billion merger with Sony Pictures Networks India, which collapsed in January 2024. Chandra later accused SEBI’s then-chair of scuttling the merger.

	In the two years since, Zee has cut roughly 15% of its workforce and expanded into sports broadcasting, striking a deal with FIFA in June for Indian broadcast and streaming rights to the 2026 and 2030 World Cups and 37 other tournaments through 2034.

	The newly approved capital is earmarked for that broader push, with the company directing the funds toward sports, acquisitions, digital content, artificial intelligence and microdrama through fiscal 2029, with sports receiving the largest share.

schema.headline: Zee Shareholders Approve $330 Million Capital Raise Before Indian Regulator Bars Company From Markets

title: Woody Harrelson to Be Honored at Sarajevo Film Festival
description: Woody Harrelson will be awarded the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival in recognition of his “outstanding contribution to
body:
Woody Harrelson will be awarded the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival in recognition of his “outstanding contribution to the film industry and an exceptional acting career,” the festival said Monday.

	The news follows announcements over the weekend that the festival would close with a newly restored version of Bosnian director Danis Tanović Oscar-winning film “No Man’s Land,” 25 years after its premiere at the Cannes Film Festival, and that Bosnian actor Emir Hadžihafizbegović would also receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.
	

	Jovan Marjanović, director of the festival, said Harrelson is “one of those actors you believe in even in the most improbable roles, while at the same time you can easily imagine him as someone you might spend time with every day.”


	He added, “That remarkable ease of performance is, in fact, one of the hardest qualities to achieve on screen, yet he delivers it film after film. His talent, charisma and boldness serve as an inspiration to many future generations.”

	Illustrating Harrelson’s versatility and prowess as an actor, the festival cited his Oscar nominations for “The People vs. Larry Flynt,” “The Messenger” and “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” and his performance in Ruben Östlund’s Palme d’Or winner “Triangle of Sadness.”

	To coincide with the award, the festival will screen Michael Winterbottom’s 1997 film “Welcome to Sarajevo.” The festival described the film as a “powerful examination of the war in Bosnia in the mid-1990s and the role of journalists in its media coverage.” It is based on journalist Michael Nicholson’s book “Natasha’s Story.” Harrelson stars alongside Stephen Dillane and Marisa Tomei.
	

	Harrelson will be seen next in Apple TV’s “Brothers” alongside Matthew McConaughey, which premieres Sept. 23, and also appears opposite Kristen Stewart in Quentin Dupieux’s “Full Phil,” which premiered at Cannes this year. He recently wrapped Netflix’s “The Cackling of the Dodos” with Sam Rockwell.

	The festival will run Aug. 14 to 21.

schema.headline: Woody Harrelson to Be Honored at Sarajevo Film Festival

title: Massive Attack Addresses Singapore Concert Aftermath in New Statement
description:
UPDATED: Massive Attack has addressed the aftermath of the Singapore concert in a statement posted to Instagram. 

	The band said its members were “
body:
UPDATED: Massive Attack has addressed the aftermath of the Singapore concert in a statement posted to Instagram. 

	The band said its members were “detained by the police, isolated and separately questioned” following the show, and described some members undergoing hotel room searches and temporary passport confiscation as part of the process. The band said the “Free Palestine” chants heard at the concert arose spontaneously from the audience, both before the performance and again at its close, and noted they had understood the flag they displayed to represent “a sovereign state recognised by 157 countries.” The group expressed appreciation for the warmth of Singaporean fans and voiced hope that citizens there would in future be able to express their views freely. The statement closed: “As we were saying … Free Palestine.”
	

	PREVIOUSLY: The two founder members of Massive Attack have been permanently barred from re-entering Singapore after unfurling a Palestinian flag during the British trip-hop group’s concert in the city-state, according to a joint statement from the Singapore Police Force and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA).


	The statement said police investigated both band members for “their actions of support for a political cause and unfurling of a foreign flag” during the show at The Star Theatre on July 29. Following the investigation, and in consultation with the Attorney-General’s Chambers, police administered stern warnings to both men for offences under Section 3 of the Foreign National Emblems (Control of Display) Act 1949 and Section 16 of the Public Order Act.
	

	“Both men will also be banned from re-entering Singapore,” the statement said.

	According to the statement, the event organizer had acknowledged the licensing conditions attached to the concert beforehand, but both band members held up a “foreign flag” onstage during the performance, with one shouting “Free Palestine.” The IMDA said it is investigating a possible breach of several licence conditions, including one barring performers from displaying flags tied to any cause, and will act once that inquiry concludes. The regulator added it will not approve any future application for the band to perform in Singapore given the entry ban.

	The concert was the band’s only scheduled Singapore date on its current tour, with video of the flag display circulating widely online alongside footage of the crowd joining in chants of “Free Palestine.” The two men are Massive Attack’s founding members, Robert “3D” Del Naja and Grant “Daddy G” Marshall, who make up its current touring lineup; authorities did not name them in the statement.

	Singapore maintains strict rules on the public display of foreign flags and emblems without a permit, framing the laws as necessary to protect the country’s racial and religious harmony. The joint statement reiterated that position, with authorities saying they “take a serious view of acts which could potentially harm the racial and religious harmony in Singapore” and urging the public, including foreigners, “to refrain from importing foreign politics” into the country.

	“The peace and harmony between different races and religions in Singapore should not be taken for granted, and we must not let external events affect our society,” the statement said.

	Massive Attack has been among the more vocal acts in music in its support for Palestinian causes. Del Naja was arrested earlier this year during a demonstration in London tied to Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the U.K.

schema.headline: Massive Attack Addresses Singapore Concert Aftermath in New Statement

title: China Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to Massive $121 Million Five-Day Opening
description: Sony Pictures’ superhero spectacle “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” swung into the top spot at the mainland China box office during the July 31–Aug. 2 we
body:
Sony Pictures’ superhero spectacle “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” swung into the top spot at the mainland China box office during the July 31–Aug. 2 weekend, generating RMB463.5 million ($68.1 million over its three-day opening frame, according to Artisan Gateway. 

	The tentpole project has grossed $121.3 million in the Middle Kingdom in its first five days of release. $19 million of this came from Imax, which makes it the highest-grossing Imax opening weekend in the “Spider-Man” franchise for China. 
	

	Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy feature “All Wishes Come True!” moved to second place in its third weekend, collecting $31.8 million. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the local hit now has a cumulative total of $171.5 million since its July 18 debut. The mythologically inspired comedy follows eight mortals who band together to outwit celestial deities and claim the mantle of the Eight Immortals.


	Shenzhen Film Studio’s sports comedy “Kung Fu Soccer” moved to third position in its fourth frame, adding $14.1 million. Directed by Stephen Chow, the runaway summer success has reached a cumulative haul of $318.5 million. The slapstick feature follows an underdog women’s soccer squad that incorporates gravity-defying martial arts maneuvers to compete for a championship title.

	Hezhong Ruike Media’s workplace comedy “Make Zhonghe Great Again” (“Johnny Keep Walking! 2”) opened in fourth place, bringing in $8.9 million over its two-day weekend frame. Including early previews prior to its Aug. 1 launch, the satirical feature has accumulated $12.4 million. Directed by Dong Runnian and starring Bai Ke, Sun Yizhou, and Zhang Ruoyun, the sequel to the 2023 hit “Johnny Keep Walking!” continues the franchise’s lampooning of internal office politics, corporate dysfunction, and the absurdities of white-collar employment.
	

	Universal’s “Obsession” rounded out the top five, collecting $4.7 million in its sophomore weekend. Directed by Curry Barker, the film has reached a cumulative total of $14.5 million.

	Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses reached $132.3 million, while the 2026 year-to-date revenue stands at $3.39 billion, down 32% from the same period in 2025.

schema.headline: China Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to Massive $121 Million Five-Day Opening

title: Erik Poppe’s ‘Beloved’ to Open Haugesund: ‘All Eyes Are on Norway,’ Says Festival Chief Tonje Hardersen
description: After the World Cup where Norway made a splash with its wealth of soccer talent – led by Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard – the Nordic nation will
body:
After the World Cup where Norway made a splash with its wealth of soccer talent – led by Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard – the Nordic nation will be showcasing some of its biggest film talents at the 54th edition of the Norwegian International Film Festival in Haugesund, running Aug. 22-28. 

	Out of 84 feature length and 20 short films in the program, 22 Norwegian features and 15 shorts made the cut, including “Beloved” (“Kjærast”) by acclaimed Oscar-shortlisted Erik Poppe (“The Kings Choice,” “A Thousand Times Goodnight,” “The Emigrants”). The drama, repped internationally by Reinvent Yellow, will have its world premiere in the picturesque Norwegian coast town Aug. 23, as its opening film.Based on the only original screenplay by Nobel Prize-winning author Jon Fosse, the film stars Leo Magnus de la Nuez (“Beforeigners”) and Kristi-Helene Giæver Engeberg (“War Sailor”) as Asle and Gerd, who live an idyllic life with their son in a small Norwegian coastal town. But soon their perfect love is put to test, as Asle, a sailor, is inexorably drawn by the call of the sea.

	Festival director Tonje Hardersen said “Beloved’ is the perfect opener. “Poppe opened the festival two years ago with “Quisling – The Final Days;” he’s a true Haugesund regular, and Jon Fosse was actually born in Haugesund, so we’re thrilled to have them with us with a powerful film, set in the dazzlingly beautiful Western Norwegian landscape.”


	“Beloved” is a love story full of the unspoken, tenderness, and mystery, unmistakably Jon Fosse,” said Poppe before adding: “We live in a time where much of what we see on film and series depicts cynicism and human distance. Perhaps the most radical thing we can do now is to tell stories about closeness and hope.”

	The pic is produced by Poppe’s regular partner Finn Gjerdrum of SF Studios’ banner Paradox.Another hotly anticipated new Norwegian film, picked for the closing gala, is “The Murder of Benjamin,” based on the real-life murder of Benjamin Hermansen, a 15-year-old boy of mixed Norwegian and Malian heritage, who was brutally murdered by a neo-Nazi in 2001.  
	

	Repped by TrustNordisk, the drama is helmed by Ingvild Søderlind, credited for Netflix’ “Royalteen: Princess Margrethe” and “Battle: Frestyle.” Seasoned Thomas Robsahm (“The Worst Person in the World,” “Lovable”) produces for Nordisk Film Production Norway. 

	“It’s a strong film that follows the dramatic racially-motivated murder that happened 25 years ago. For me it was yesterday, but the younger generation doesn’t know about it which is why it’s key to highlight it at Haugesund,” said Hardersen.

	Cracks in Norwegian society

	The festival chief noted that cracks in Norwegian society is a predominant theme this year, tackled as well in Jørgen Nordby’s Norwegian doc-feature “The Voice That Vanished,” a world premiere. The pic follows local artist Helene Bøksle and the traumatic experience of having her vocals from the game “Age of Conan” used by the July 22, 2011 mass murderer Anders Behring Breivik in his propaganda videos. Then in Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” one of a handful Cannes competition entries secured by Hardersen (with “Fatherland,” “Parallel Tales” and “The Beloved”), it’s the turn of Norway’s child protection system to come in for scrutiny. 

	“I’m really curious to see how the film will go down at the very first screening with a national audience,” said Hardersen. Mungiu will walk the Haugesund red carpet Aug. 25, when his Cannes winner opens New Nordic Films, the festival’s industry sidebar and biggest Nordic Film Market of the year, together with the twin event Nordic Film Market at Göteborg.

	As underscored by the fest honcho, “Fjord” stars Renate Reinsve who toplines Haugesund’s other local pick “Butterfly” by Itonje Søimer Guttormsen, and the Oscar winner “Sentimental Value.” 

	Screening at the Amanda Nominees sidebar, Joachim Trier’s family drama has a chance to make history at the Norway’s Amanda national film awards if he coverts all its 12 nods into wins Aug. 22 at Haugesund’s Festiviteten Concert Hall.

	Besides Mungiu, A-list talent expected take in “Game of Thrones”’ Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, a producer together with Norway’s Kristian Landmark on the Greenlandic-set documentary “Qajaq Man,” and local household name Anders Danielsen Lie (“The Worst Person in the World”), whose performance as jazz legend Bill Evans in the Berlin Silver Bear winner “Everybody Digs Bill Evans” enthused critics, including Variety’s.
	

	Danielsen Lie will be honored at Haugesund alongside film and theatre actress Anne Marie Ottesen, when their names will be added to the festival’s Walk of Fame at a ceremony Aug. 22. 

	Among the festival’s top non-competitive sections, the Nordic Focus will screen 10 new titles including Finnish chiller “Nightborn” and Danish gothic gay romance “No Rest for the Wicked” which scooped two top awards each at the recent Fantasia Film Fest; Haugesund’s parallel children’s festival Cinemagi will open with the Norwegian kids movie “Back To Tottori,” sequel to Silje Salomonsen and Arild Østin Ommundsen’s 2021 Amanda winner “Sisters: The Summer We Found Our Superpowers.”

	All Eyes on Norway

	“Our cinema is strong, and after the World Cup, all eyes are on Norway. We’re enjoying a unique momentum with which to further boost our films and country as a film nation. However, our audiovisual sector as a whole is still struggling, with many people losing their jobs,” commented Hardersen, who said the topic of how to strengthen the Norwegian industry in the next decade will be one of the main themes of Haugesund’s Film Policy Conference on Aug. 23. “We’re not part of the E.U. and don’t want to be left out when the E.U. launches its flagship [2028-2034] AgoraEU program,” she said.

	As for the Norwegian International Film Festival which she has headed since 2015, Hardersen is pleased to announce that it has consolidated its brand in 2026 by expanding its footprint to Stavanger, the Rogaland region’s largest city and Norway’s oil capital. 

	The Stavanger Festival’s soft launch last March sold more than 10,000 tickets and boosted the Norwegian International Film Festival’s overall visitors by 30%. “As Stavanger’s first film festival, we tapped into the large expat community working in the oil business and university students. It was a great experience,” said Hardersen. “Government support to our festival is based on our ability to renew ourselves, and the Stavanger film event was also a way to give back to our key backer, the Rogaland County.”  

	Would she be tempted in the future to move the must-attend industry showcase New Nordic Films to Stavanger, four times the size of Haugesund? “No”, she said. “The beauty and uniqueness of Haugesund is its small size. You run into everyone. This two-city Norwegian film festival allows us to keep cinemas active in our region, to build new audiences and for our staff to be employed all-year round.”

schema.headline: Erik Poppe’s ‘Beloved’ to Open Haugesund: ‘All Eyes Are on Norway,’ Says Festival Chief Tonje Hardersen

title: Korea Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut
description: Superhero blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has delivered a huge opening at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Jul. 31–Aug. 2.
body:
Superhero blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has delivered a huge opening at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Jul. 31–Aug. 2. 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the web-slinging sequel generated a colossal $16.9 million from 2,252,930 admissions over the three-day frame across 2,409 screens, capturing an overwhelming 80.63% share of total weekend revenue. Since launching wide on July 29, the tentpole has pulled in a cumulative gross of $25 million from 3,384,147 total admissions. Of this, Imax accounted for $2.4 million, making it the highest grossing Imax opening weekend of all time in the territory. 
	

	The arrival of the superhero juggernaut ended the two-week streak of local sci-fi survival thriller “Hope,” which moved to second place. The Na Hong-Jin-directed epic starring Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Michael Fassbender, and Alicia Vikander brought in $2.4 million from 335,810 admissions over the frame. The film has now accumulated a total of $31 million from 4,110,550 admissions since its July 15 launch.


	“Minions & Monsters” finished in third place, adding $434,409 from 65,245 ticket buyers over the weekend frame. The film has raised its total to $5 million from 713,940 admissions.

	“Moana” was in fourth place in its fourth weekend of release, collecting $252,794 from 37,122 admissions. The oceanic adventure has reached a total local gross of $7.4 million from 999,949 admissions.

	“Toy Story 5” placed fifth, adding $222,465 from 31,874 admissions. The family blockbuster has now amassed a cumulative South Korean gross of $20.9 million from 2,912,210 total admissions since its mid-June debut.
	

	Faith-based animated feature “David” took sixth place, generating $167,794 from 25,013 admissions over the frame, pushing its haul to $1.7 million from 263,378 viewers.

	Local animated sequel “Teenieping: Legend of the Whale Heartstone” landed in seventh place ahead of its official release, bringing in $177,482 from 20,986 admissions across preview screenings. Directed by Kim Soo-hoon, the musical fantasy sequel to the 2024 hit animated film follows Princess Romi and her fairy companion Heartsping as they dive into an ocean journey to rescue Queen Velita from deep-sea creatures. Including early previews, the family film has collected $215,104 from 26,494 tickets.

	Tomoaki Fujino’s “What Should We Have Done?” debuted in eighth place, pulling in $116,603 from 16,009 admissions over the weekend. The acclaimed documentary captures a 20-year personal chronicle of a family struggling with severe mental illness and social isolation. Since its Jul. 29 premiere, the release has grossed $170,552 from 24,008 viewers.

	Local psychological thriller “The Eyes,” directed by Yeom Ji-ho and starring Shin Min-ah and Kim Nam-hee, took ninth place with $55,396 from 7,364 admissions, stretching its overall local cume to $11.1 million from 1,537,378 tickets.

	Rounding out the top 10 was the Japanese anime feature “Dream Animals The Movie,” which added $30,263 from 4,719 admissions over its second frame to bring its gross to $262,973 from 41,996 ticket buyers.

	The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $20.8 million, making it the biggest weekend of the year, soaring above last week’s $8.2 million.

title: Modest Mouse Pulls Guitarist From Tour After Alleged DMs to Teen Surface
description:
Modest Mouse Guitarist
                          Booted From Tour Over Alleged DMs to Teen
body:
Modest Mouse Guitarist
                          Booted From Tour Over Alleged DMs to Teen
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                August 2, 2026
                
                            3:30 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 2, 2026
                                4:48 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Modest Mouse guitarist Simon O'Connor is sitting out the band's next tour after allegedly sliding into an underage fan's DMs with an explicit image ... then telling her a night of partying -- and her bikini pics -- helped spark the exchange.
      
    
            The fan shared screenshots on Reddit showing messages O'Connor allegedly sent before her 17th birthday. She claims her age was clearly displayed on her Instagram bio at the time.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Take a look through the DMs ... the alleged exchange starts with O'Connor sending a meme and a sexually explicit image, prompting the teen to ask whether he'd been hacked.
      

            O'Connor allegedly said he hadn't been hacked and blamed the messages on a "party night" ... before suggesting the fan's bikini photos had also caught his attention.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The guitarist -- who joined the band in 2021 and played on their latest album, "An Eraser and a Maze"-- later posted his own lengthy explanation on the Modest Mouse subreddit ... saying he mistook the teen for someone who had repeatedly harassed and pranked him through fake accounts.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            O'Connor admitted he used "poor judgement" when he fired off what he called a tasteless meme and a "Simon calls your bluff" sticker ... but said he unsent the messages and ended the conversation once he realized he had the wrong person.
      
    
            He apologized to the fan ... saying she didn't deserve to be put in that position, and said he strongly opposes any sexual behavior involving minors.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Modest Mouse has since announced O'Connor won't join its upcoming North American tour, which kicks off Tuesday in Ojai, California ... Seth Jabour of Les Savy Fav will step in on guitar in his place.
      
    
            The band didn't clarify whether O'Connor is gone for good ... but for now, he's definitely not floating on with the tour.
      
    
            We've reached out to the band's reps ... so far, no word back.
